chapter_title: Theory of Computation and Computer Graphics

topics.title: Finite Automata (FA) & Determinism
topics.content:
Core Concepts:
- Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA): Defined by tuple $(Q, \Sigma, \delta, q_0, F)$[cite: 1]. Every state has exactly one transition per input symbol[cite: 1].
- Non-Deterministic Finite Automaton (NFA/NDFA): Allows multiple next states for a single symbol and optional $\epsilon$-transitions[cite: 1].
- Equivalence: NFAs and DFAs have equal language recognition power[cite: 1]. An $n$-state NFA converts to an equivalent DFA with at most $2^n$ states via subset construction[cite: 1].
- Minimization: Removes unreachable/redundant states using Hopcroft's or table-filling methods to produce a unique minimal DFA[cite: 1].

topics.title: Regular Expressions (RE) & Pumping Lemma
topics.content:
Regular Expressions:
- Basic operators: Concatenation ($ab$), Union ($a|b$ or $a+b$), and Kleene star ($a^*$)[cite: 1].
- Expressive Equivalence: RE $\equiv$ FA (Kleene's Theorem)[cite: 1]. Recognizes Regular Languages[cite: 1].

Pumping Lemma for Regular Languages:
- Used exclusively to prove a language is NOT regular[cite: 1].
- Lemma statement: If $L$ is regular, there exists a length $p$ such that any string $s \in L$ with $|s| \ge p$ can be written as $s = xyz$ satisfying $|xy| \le p$, $|y| > 0$, and $xy^i z \in L$ for all $i \ge 0$[cite: 1].
- Classic non-regular examples: $\{0^n 1^n \mid n \ge 0\}$ and $\{ww \mid w \in \{0,1\}^*\}$[cite: 1].

topics.title: Context-Free Grammar (CFG) & Parsing
topics.content:
Grammar Structure & Derivations:
- Defined by $(V, T, P, S)$ where production rules have a single non-terminal on the left ($V \rightarrow w$)[cite: 1].
- Derivations: Leftmost (replaces leftmost non-terminal first) and Rightmost[cite: 1].
- Parse Trees: Graphical representation of derivations[cite: 1]. Leaves represent terminals[cite: 1].
- Ambiguity: A grammar is ambiguous if a string has two or more distinct parse trees (or leftmost derivations)[cite: 1].

Normal Forms & Notation:
- Chomsky Normal Form (CNF): Productions are $A \rightarrow BC$ or $A \rightarrow a$[cite: 1].
- Greibach Normal Form (GNF): Productions are $A \rightarrow a\alpha$[cite: 1].
- Backus-Naur Form (BNF): Standard notation for describing programming language syntax[cite: 1].

topics.title: Pushdown Automata (PDA) & CFL Properties
topics.content:
Pushdown Automata (PDA):
- PDA = Finite Automaton + Stack Memory[cite: 1].
- Handles nested structures (e.g., $\{a^n b^n \mid n \ge 0\}$)[cite: 1].
- Equivalence: Languages accepted by PDAs $\equiv$ Context-Free Languages (CFLs) generated by CFGs[cite: 1].

Pumping Lemma & Closure Properties for CFLs:
- Pumping Lemma for CFLs: Any string $s$ with $|s| \ge p$ splits as $uvxyz$ where $|vxy| \le p$, $|vy| > 0$, and $uv^i xy^i z \in L$ for all $i \ge 0$[cite: 1]. Non-CFL examples: $\{a^n b^n c^n\}$ and $\{ww\}$[cite: 1].
- Closure: CFLs are closed under Union, Concatenation, Kleene Star, and Reversal[cite: 1]. CFLs are NOT closed under Intersection or Complement[cite: 1].

topics.title: Turing Machine (TM) Architecture & Variants
topics.content:
TM Fundamentals:
- Architecture: Infinite read/write tape, tape head moving Left (L) or Right (R), and finite state control[cite: 1].
- Languages: Decidable/Recursive (TM halts and correctly accepts/rejects all inputs) vs. Recognizable/Recursively Enumerable (TM accepts valid inputs, may loop endlessly on invalid inputs)[cite: 1].
- Variants: Multi-Track TM, Multi-Tape TM, and Non-Deterministic TM (NTM)[cite: 1]. All variants are equivalent in computational power to a standard single-tape TM[cite: 1].

Theses and Universal Models:
- Church-Turing Thesis: Informal belief that any algorithmically computable function can be computed by a Turing Machine[cite: 1].
- Universal Turing Machine (UTM): A TM that simulates any arbitrary TM by reading its description and input from the tape[cite: 1].

topics.title: Complexity, Reducibility & Intractability
topics.content:
Complexity Classes:
- Time Complexity: Number of steps taken by a TM[cite: 1]. Class P (Polynomial time $O(n^k)$)[cite: 1]. Class NP (Verifiable in polynomial time)[cite: 1].
- NP-Complete: Hardest problems in NP[cite: 1]. NP-Hard: At least as hard as NP-Complete problems[cite: 1].

Reducibility & Decidability:
- Reduction ($A \le B$): If $A$ reduces to $B$ and $B$ is decidable, then $A$ is decidable[cite: 1]. If $A$ is undecidable, $B$ is undecidable[cite: 1].
- Undecidable Problems: Halting Problem (determining if a TM halts on input $w$)[cite: 1] and Rice's Theorem properties[cite: 1].

topics.title: Graphics Hardware & Display Architecture
topics.content:
Display Technologies:
- Raster-Scan Display: Scans line-by-line horizontally; uses a Frame Buffer to store pixel color/intensity values[cite: 1]. Suffers from aliasing[cite: 1].
- Vector (Random-Scan) Display: Draws lines directly between endpoints driven by a display command list[cite: 1]. Produces smooth lines without aliasing[cite: 1].
- Technologies: CRT, LCD, LED, and OLED (self-emitting pixels, high contrast)[cite: 1].

Hardware Components & Standards:
- GPU & Display Processors: Offloads graphics rendering, scan conversion, clipping, and transformations from CPU[cite: 1].
- Graphics APIs/Standards: GKS (2D standard)[cite: 1], PHIGS (hierarchical 3D)[cite: 1], OpenGL (cross-platform 2D/3D API)[cite: 1], DirectX, and Vulkan[cite: 1].

topics.title: 2D Affine Transformations & Homogeneous Coordinates
topics.content:
Homogeneous Coordinates:
- Represents 2D points as 3D vectors $(x, y, 1)$ to allow translation to be expressed as matrix multiplication[cite: 1].

Transformation Matrices (3x3):
- Translation: $x' = x + t_x$, $y' = y + t_y$[cite: 1].
- Rotation (counter-clockwise by $\theta$ about origin): $x' = x \cos\theta - y \sin\theta$, $y' = x \sin\theta + y \cos\theta$[cite: 1].
- Scaling: $x' = x \cdot s_x$, $y' = y \cdot s_y$[cite: 1]. Uniform if $s_x = s_y$[cite: 1].
- Reflection: $y$-axis ($x' = -x, y' = y$), $x$-axis ($x' = x, y' = -y$), Origin ($x' = -x, y' = -y$), Line $y=x$ ($x' = y, y' = x$)[cite: 1].
- Shear: Horizontal ($x' = x + sh_x \cdot y$), Vertical ($y' = y + sh_y \cdot x$)[cite: 1].
- Composite Transformations: Achieved via matrix multiplication (applied right-to-left)[cite: 1]. Matrix multiplication is non-commutative ($A \times B \neq B \times A$)[cite: 1].

topics.title: 2D Viewing Pipeline & Line Clipping Algorithms
topics.content:
Viewing Pipeline:
- World Coordinates $\rightarrow$ Viewing Coordinates $\rightarrow$ Normalized Coordinates $\rightarrow$ Device/Screen Coordinates (via Window-to-Viewport mapping)[cite: 1].

Line Clipping Algorithms:
- Cohen-Sutherland: Uses 4-bit region codes (Top, Bottom, Right, Left) for 9 regions[cite: 1]. Trivial accept if both codes are $0000$[cite: 1]; trivial reject if bitwise AND $\neq 0000$[cite: 1]. Otherwise calculates boundary intersections iteratively[cite: 1].
- Liang-Barsky: Parametric line clipping algorithm ($x = x_1 + t\Delta x$, $y = y_1 + t\Delta y$)[cite: 1]. Solves $t \cdot p_k \le q_k$ inequalities[cite: 1]. More computationally efficient than Cohen-Sutherland[cite: 1].

topics.title: 3D Transformations & Homogeneous Representation
topics.content:
3D Homogeneous Matrix (4x4):
- Translation: Shifts $(x, y, z)$ by $(t_x, t_y, t_z)$ using 4x4 matrices[cite: 1].
- Rotation: Axis-specific rotation matrices ($R_x(\theta)$, $R_y(\theta)$, $R_z(\theta)$)[cite: 1]. Note: Rotation around $Y$-axis has inverted sign terms for sine ($x' = x \cos\theta + z \sin\theta$, $z' = -x \sin\theta + z \cos\theta$)[cite: 1].
- Scaling & Reflection: 3D diagonal scaling ($s_x, s_y, s_z$)[cite: 1]; Reflection across principal planes ($XY, XZ, YZ$)[cite: 1].
- 3D Shear: 6 possible directional parameter combinations[cite: 1].

topics.title: 3D Viewing Pipeline & Projection Techniques
topics.content:
Projection Types:
- Parallel Projection: Projection rays are parallel[cite: 1]. Preserves relative proportions and parallel lines (no foreshortening)[cite: 1].
  - Orthographic: Rays perpendicular to projection plane[cite: 1]. Includes Multiview (Front, Top, Side) and Axonometric (Isometric: 120° angles, Dimetric, Trimetric)[cite: 1].
  - Oblique: Rays intersect projection plane at an angle[cite: 1]. Includes Cavalier (angle 45°, full depth factor) and Cabinet (angle 63.4°, depth factor halved)[cite: 1].
- Perspective Projection: Rays converge at Center of Projection (COP)[cite: 1]. Features foreshortening (distant objects appear smaller)[cite: 1]. Classified by 1, 2, or 3 vanishing points[cite: 1]. Uses a frustum viewing volume[cite: 1].

questions.question: What does DFA stand for in Theory of Computation?
questions.explanation: DFA stands for Deterministic Finite Automaton[cite: 1].

questions.question: In a DFA, how many next states are permitted for a specific state and input symbol?
questions.explanation: A DFA is deterministic, meaning every state has exactly one defined transition per input symbol[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which class of languages is recognized by Finite Automata?
questions.explanation: Finite Automata accept Regular Languages[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Pumping Lemma for regular languages?
options: To prove a language is regular
To prove a language is NOT regular
questions.explanation: The Pumping Lemma for regular languages is used as a proof technique to demonstrate that a language is not regular[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which algorithm is used to convert an NFA into an equivalent DFA?
questions.explanation: Subset Construction converts an NFA into an equivalent DFA by assigning each DFA state to a set of NFA states[cite: 1].

questions.question: If an NFA has 4 states, what is the maximum number of states its equivalent minimal or non-minimal DFA can have?
questions.explanation: For an $n$-state NFA, the power set construction produces a DFA with up to $2^n$ states ($2^4 = 16$)[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the defining production characteristic of a Context-Free Grammar (CFG)?
options: Left side has a single non-terminal variable
Left side contains terminals and non-terminals
Right side must contain only terminals
questions.explanation: In a CFG, production rules are of the form $V \rightarrow w$, where $V$ is a single non-terminal variable[cite: 1].

questions.question: A grammar that produces more than one distinct parse tree for a single string is called:
questions.explanation: An ambiguous grammar generates multiple parse trees or leftmost derivations for at least one string in its language[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which production format corresponds to Chomsky Normal Form (CNF)?
questions.explanation: In CNF, all productions are strictly of the form $A \rightarrow BC$ (two non-terminals) or $A \rightarrow a$ (single terminal)[cite: 1].

questions.question: What extra memory component distinguishes a Pushdown Automaton (PDA) from a Finite Automaton (FA)?
questions.explanation: A PDA adds a stack memory to a finite automaton[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which language class is recognized by Pushdown Automata?
questions.explanation: Pushdown Automata recognize Context-Free Languages[cite: 1].

questions.question: Context-Free Languages are NOT closed under which of the following operations?
questions.explanation: CFLs are closed under union, concatenation, and Kleene star, but are NOT closed under intersection or complement[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which computational model possesses an infinite read/write tape?
questions.explanation: A Turing Machine uses an infinite read/write tape as its primary memory[cite: 1].

questions.question: A Turing Machine that is guaranteed to halt on every input string is called a:
questions.explanation: A Decider is a Turing Machine that always halts on all inputs, accepting or rejecting[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which of the following problems is famous for being undecidable?
questions.explanation: The Halting Problem (determining whether an arbitrary TM halts on a given input) is proven undecidable[cite: 1].

questions.question: What does the Church-Turing Thesis state?
options: Any algorithmically computable function can be computed by a Turing Machine
questions.explanation: The Church-Turing Thesis posits that Turing Machines formalize the intuitive concept of effective algorithmic computation[cite: 1].

questions.question: Class P in complexity theory includes problems solvable in:
questions.explanation: Class P comprises decision problems solvable by a deterministic TM in polynomial time $O(n^k)$[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which display technology continuously scans line-by-line horizontally using a frame buffer?
questions.explanation: Raster-scan displays scan pixel grid lines row-by-row using pixel data stored in a frame buffer[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which graphics API is an open, cross-platform standard for 2D/3D rendering?
questions.explanation: OpenGL is an open, cross-platform API industry standard for 2D and 3D graphics rendering[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the primary reason for using Homogeneous Coordinates (x, y, 1) in 2D transformations?
options: To express translation as matrix multiplication
questions.explanation: Homogeneous coordinates enable translation to be implemented via 3x3 matrix multiplication rather than addition, allowing unified composite operations[cite: 1].

questions.question: In 2D rotation about the origin by angle θ, what is the transformed coordinate x'?
questions.explanation: The standard 2D counter-clockwise rotation formula for $x'$ is $x' = x \cos\theta - y \sin\theta$[cite: 1].

questions.question: A 2D scaling transformation with factors sx = 2 and sy = 1 results in:
questions.explanation: When $s_x \neq s_y$, non-uniform scaling occurs, stretching the object horizontally[cite: 1].

questions.question: Reflection of point (x, y) across the x-axis yields which new coordinates?
questions.explanation: Reflection across the x-axis keeps $x$ identical while negating $y$ ($(x, -y)$)[cite: 1].

questions.question: In the Cohen-Sutherland line clipping algorithm, what region code represents a point inside the window?
questions.explanation: Region code $0000$ indicates that a point lies inside all four window boundaries[cite: 1].

questions.question: In Cohen-Sutherland clipping, if the bitwise AND of two endpoint region codes is non-zero, the line is:
questions.explanation: A non-zero bitwise AND indicates both endpoints share an exterior region outside the same boundary, so the line is trivially rejected[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which line clipping algorithm uses parametric equations and is computationally more efficient than Cohen-Sutherland?
questions.explanation: The Liang-Barsky algorithm uses parametric line representations and reduces unnecessary intersection calculations[cite: 1].

questions.question: What size is the matrix representation for 3D homogeneous transformations?
questions.explanation: 3D homogeneous transformations are represented using 4x4 matrices[cite: 1].

questions.question: In 3D projection, which type ensures parallel lines remain parallel and does not exhibit foreshortening?
questions.explanation: Parallel projection keeps parallel lines parallel and preserves true dimensions without depth foreshortening[cite: 1].

questions.question: An Oblique projection where the projection angle is 45° and d' = d (no depth reduction) is known as:
questions.explanation: Cavalier projection uses a 45° projection angle, preserving full depth without scale reduction[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which projection method simulates human vision by causing distant objects to appear smaller?
questions.explanation: Perspective projection features foreshortening where object dimensions shrink proportionally with distance from the viewer[cite: 1].
